name: Centru
tagline: Stefan cel Mare boulevard and everything off it
description: The centre of Chisinau along its main boulevard, with the City Hall, the cathedral in its park, the triumphal arch and most of the restaurants and bars. It is flat, laid out on a Russian imperial grid and entirely walkable.
bestFor: Anyone who wants to live without a car in the middle of the city
pros: Cathedral park and the central market
cons: The most expensive area in Chisinau, which is not saying much

name: Botanica
tagline: The green southern district with the botanical garden
description: A large residential district south of the centre, built out in the Soviet period, with the Botanical Garden, Valea Trandafirilor park and a great deal of tree cover. It is quieter and cheaper than the centre and well connected by trolleybus.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting parks and lower rent
pros: The Botanical Garden and Valea Trandafirilor
cons: Fifteen to twenty minutes from the centre

name: Riscani
tagline: North of the centre, by the lake
description: A residential district north of the railway with Valea Morilor park and its lake nearby, a mix of Soviet blocks and newer construction, and good trolleybus links. It is where a lot of Chisinau's newer apartment building has happened.
bestFor: Anyone wanting newer housing at a reasonable price
pros: Newer apartment stock than the centre
cons: Character is functional rather than attractive
Ten to fifteen minutes from the centre

name: Telecentru
tagline: The hilly western district, quieter and residential
description: A residential area west of the centre on rising ground, with a mix of private houses and low-rise blocks and more greenery than the Soviet districts. It is quieter, a little more expensive than Botanica and popular with families.
bestFor: Anyone wanting a house or a quiet street near the centre
pros: Quieter and greener than the eastern districts

name: Cricova and the Wine Roads
tagline: Half an hour out, and underground
description: The village north of the city whose limestone quarries became a wine cellar with over a hundred kilometres of underground streets, named after the wines stored along them. Milestii Mici, further south, holds the largest wine collection in the world.
bestFor: Anyone whose interest in Moldova is the wine
pros: Rural quiet half an hour from the capital
cons: A car or a tour is needed
